transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood), Markus Li (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Redwood CSM); Priya Malhotra (Aurora CTO), James O'Neill (Aurora SRE Lead), Sara Kim (Aurora Eng Mgr), Elena Ruiz (Aurora Security), Michael Tan (Aurora Product)

---
Summary: Quick recap of Feb 9 incident: spike in tail latency ~30-45 minutes during batch job, several model servers reported transient OOM and reclaimed cache; automated fallback kicked in but disruption of ~7 minutes for a subset of requests.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have most of the folks, we'll run 40ish minutes. quick agenda, timeline review, rca, mitigations, owners. Priya you good to kick off?
[00:12] Priya Malhotra: yeah thanks Lena, hey team. so feb 9 black friday-like... uh not black friday but high volume batch run, we saw elevated latencies and some errors coming from inference endpoints. James can show data but our consumers saw retries and product alerts, so started escalation.
[00:31] James O'Neill: yep, i pulled traces - about 10% of requests in a particular route hit > 1.5s lat, typical p99 is 350ms. there were also 503s logged; looked correlated to a single dedicated pool that hit gpu memory pressure.
[00:48] Markus Li: thanks james. preliminary from our side, we saw KV cache evictions increase rapidly when sequence length distribution shifted; continuous batching combined with a jump in concurrent prefixes caused memory blowout on a few nodes. we had fallback model variant come up but that increased CPU decoding and cost.
[01:05] Sara Kim: to clarify, when you say prefixes, do you mean session state/kv? our workload had a new experiment that sends long context for few users. could that be it?
[01:21] Markus Li: yeah exactly, longer context = bigger KV footprint per session. the autoscaler didn't spin up enough additional workers fast enough given the sudden memory churn.
[01:34] Priya Malhotra: okay so is the main root cause cache + autoscale latency or is there a kernel/quantization bug?
[01:41] Markus Li: we considered a kernel bug but logs point to memory churn pattern from kv cache and batching. there was also a minor regression in one of our memory accounting metrics that delayed eviction thresholds by a few seconds, exacerbating the churn.
[01:57] Elena Ruiz: from a security/audit perspective we need to capture the timeline and retention. did any PII leave logs or were there expanded debug traces?
[02:06] Aisha Rahman: quick answer - no PII was in the debug traces we captured. we did enable additional debug level for 15 minutes during the incident, logs are in the incident bundle we will share.
[02:17] Michael Tan: product impact for us was roughly 7 minutes of degraded performance for some enterprise customers, some automatic retries masked errors but increased cost. that's what triggered procurement concerns.
[02:32] Lena Ortiz: ok thanks. next up immediate mitigations applied during incident? Markus?
[02:36] Markus Li: we applied three quick mitigations: 1) tightened KV cache eviction thresholds manually to free up memory; 2) temporarily reduced max batch size to reduce per-request memory footprint; 3) rolled back a config change that increased prefetching. these reduced pressure within about 4-5 minutes.
[02:58] James O'Neill: i can confirm latency dropped after the config rollback and eviction adjustments. we saw more stable memory usage afterwards.
[03:06] Priya Malhotra: good. for the patch plan, what's the short-term fix versus longer-term?
[03:11] Markus Li: short-term: patch to memory accounting regression (simple fix, ETA 4 business days), automatic cap on per-session KV growth, and adjust autoscaler thresholds to react faster to cache churn. long-term: better telemetry for KV cache by prefix, smarter eviction heuristics, and a canary runway for prefix-heavy workloads.
[03:28] Sara Kim: can the patch be applied without service restart? we can't afford downtime.
[03:33] Markus Li: yes most of the fixes are hotpatchable; the memory accounting fix can be rolled in a config + lightweight restart for a subset of nodes, we'll do canary and staggered restarts.
[03:45] Priya Malhotra: great. a few compliance questions - what logs did you capture and how long will they be retained?
[03:52] Aisha Rahman: we captured debug traces and kernel OOM logs for 30 minutes around the incident, and we'll provide sanitized bundles to Aurora. retention policy is configurable; for this incident we will keep raw bundles for 30 days unless Aurora requests longer.
[04:08] Elena Ruiz: we need 90-day retention for audit - can you accommodate that? Also need assurance of encryption at rest with our KMS.
[04:16] Lena Ortiz: yes we can extend retention for Aurora as part of enterprise package, and Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for private deployments. we'll include those options in the follow-up security package.
[04:27] Michael Tan: cost impact from fallbacks - can you approximate incremental cost for that 7-minute period?
[04:33] Markus Li: rough estimate: fallback decoding on CPU increased token cost by ~3x for the affected requests; across your traffic window that's an estimated incremental charge of about $1.2k for that period. we'll provide exact numbers in the cost appendix.
[04:51] Priya Malhotra: okay, for the root cause statement, do we want to capture it as: traffic pattern change (long prefixes) + KV cache accounting regression + autoscaler reaction lag = transient memory pressure -> OOMs and fallback?
[05:05] James O'Neill: that matches our read.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. next, testing and validation - Aurora asked for joint benchmark. Markus can you outline the plan?
[05:16] Markus Li: propose three staged tests: 1) reproduce load profile with a controlled prefix length distribution; 2) instrument KV cache telemetry to observe evictions and mem usage; 3) run the patched config with canary nodes and validate no regressions. we'll set up a shared benchmark sheet and synthetic workload repo.
[05:34] Sara Kim: will you need our S3 traces or synthetic generator?
[05:38] Markus Li: your traces are ideal if you can share sanitized samples; otherwise we'll use generated traffic but prefer real tail behavior.
[05:45] Priya Malhotra: i'll assign James to share a sanitized trace set. James?
[05:49] James O'Neill: yep i'll export the trace subset and upload to the shared bucket, obfuscating user ids, target due date 2027-02-19.
[05:58] Aisha Rahman: i'll assemble the incident deck and incident bundle and share by 2027-02-16.
[06:03] Elena Ruiz: on the security side, we'll review the debug log bundle before it's shared widely and provide redaction guidance.
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: excellent. any open questions or objections?
[06:14] Michael Tan: one lingering question - will Redwood change the autoscale policy globally or only for us?
[06:20] Markus Li: we'll propose a patch that is configurable per-customer routing/pool; default policy won't change immediately. For now we'll propose per-pool overrides for Aurora, can be rolled to defaults after validation.
[06:31] Priya Malhotra: timeline constraints: procurement wants proof that this won't reoccur. can we provide a verification plan with clear pass/fail criteria?
[06:38] Markus Li: yes pass criteria: sustained p99 < 500ms under your peak load profile, zero OOMs across canary nodes for 1 hour, and KV cache eviction metrics within expected thresholds. we'll run tests and provide results.
[06:50] Sara Kim: what about alerting changes - we want better early warning for kv churn.
[06:55] Markus Li: we can add an early warning alert based on eviction rate and rising mem footprint per prefix; simple rule-based alert first, then refine with ML if needed.
[07:06] Priya Malhotra: okay that's helpful. can we capture next steps now?
[07:10] Lena Ortiz: yes recap - action items: markus share telemetry + patch ETA, aisha send incident bundle, james share traces, priy a to confirm audit needs. then schedule bench week of 2/22 and verification call last week of february.
[07:28] Michael Tan: all good from product side.
[07:30] Priya Malhotra: thanks everyone appreciate the quick response.
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: thanks all we'll follow up in email with timeline and deck.
[07:37] (call ends)
